run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation app is up (18 pods Running, 0 restarts) except for the search backend: the search Deployment has 0 ready/available replicas and no search pod exists, so the frontend's HTTP GET /hotels returns 500 on every sampled request, each failing on its child client span /search.Search/Nearby (10-47us, ERROR) while /recommendations, POST /reservation and POST /user return 200. The search ReplicaSet cannot recreate the pod because a ResourceQuota named memory-limit-quota (created in namespace hotel-reservation at 01:45:02Z, spec.hard memory=1Gi, status.used memory=0) rejects it with 'must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search'; the search container (like every container in all 19 deployments) declares only cpu requests/limits and no memory. The prior search pod logged 'Successfully registered in consul' at 01:44:52 and its container was stopped at 01:45:03; since then every replacement pod is refused (10 FailedCreate events 01:45:04-01:45:05). Impact is confined to the search backend and the /hotels page that depends on it; reservation, user, profile and recommendation paths were checked and show successful 200 responses.

claims.text: In namespace hotel-reservation the Deployment 'search' has spec.replicas=1 but status.readyReplicas and status.availableReplicas are null, and its conditions include Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable, lastTransitionTime 2026-11-24T01:45:03Z) and ReplicaFailure=True with message 'pods "search-567bb6c4b8-j5hr4" is forbidden: failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search'.

No search pod exists: the namespace pod list contains 18 pods, all Running with restartCount 0, and none of them belongs to the search Deployment; the corresponding Endpoints object 'search' has no subsets, while the 'search' Service still exposes ports 8082 and 9092.

ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 (desired 1 replica, 0 ready) carries condition ReplicaFailure=True with message 'pods "search-567bb6c4b8-j5hr4" is forbidden: failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search', and namespace events record 10 ReplicaSet FailedCreate events with that exact message between 2026-11-24T01:45:04Z and 01:45:05Z.

ResourceQuota 'memory-limit-quota' exists in namespace hotel-reservation with creationTimestamp 2026-11-24T01:45:02Z, spec.hard {"memory":"1Gi"} and status.used {"memory":"0"}; its last write is attributed to manager OpenAPI-Generator at 01:45:02Z.

The search Deployment's container 'hotel-reserv-search' declares only requests.cpu=100m and limits.cpu=1, with no memory request or limit; the same cpu-only resource pattern is present on the containers of all 19 deployments in hotel-reservation.

A search pod was serving minutes earlier: pod search-567bb6c4b8-4rhbf logged 'Trying to register service [ name: srv-search, id: e80378f4-..., address: 10.244.234.176:8082 ]' and 'Successfully registered in consul' at 2026-11-24T01:44:52Z, and the namespace events show a Normal 'Killing - Stopping container hotel-reserv-search' on that pod at 2026-11-24T01:45:03Z.

The frontend's own spans show HTTP GET /hotels failing with error=true, http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR (40 such spans in the error-tagged sample, durations 24-110us), each carrying a child client span /search.Search/Nearby with error=true and duration 10-47us; only these two operations appear among the frontend's error spans.

Other frontend paths succeeded in the same window: HTTP GET /recommendations returned http.status_code=200 (9 spans, 1238-2063us) with profile and recommendation server spans, HTTP POST /reservation returned 200 (5 spans) with reservation and user server spans, and HTTP POST /user returned 200 (4 spans) with user server spans; none of those spans is error-tagged.

Jaeger's service list for this stack is frontend, profile, recommendation, reservation and user only - no search service spans exist, consistent with the search pod being absent; the frontend's own operation list still includes the client operation /search.Search/Nearby.

Cause: ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota in namespace hotel-reservation, created 01:45:02Z with hard memory=1Gi, is what forbids creation of the replacement search pod ('failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search' while used memory is 0), which leaves the search Service with no endpoints and makes the frontend /hotels endpoint return 500.

The two FailedScheduling warnings in hotel-reservation (mongodb-geo-78487c9767-q7w8d and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-g6c9z, 01:44:52Z) are volume-binding failures on pods that their Deployments immediately replaced (SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate, scale down/up 01:44:51-01:44:53); both Deployments now run one ready pod with 0 restarts, so this is initial-rollout churn rather than an ongoing fault.

Second candidate: the search Deployment itself is the misconfigured object, because its pod template specifies no memory request/limit while the namespace quota requires memory; the same omission exists on all other deployments, so if the quota is intended to stay, any pod restart in hotel-reservation will be rejected the same way.

A runtime fault inside the search application (crash loop, bad dependency, OOM) is rejected as the explanation of the outage: no search container is running at all (no pod, no endpoints, no search spans), the previous container's log ends with a clean startup and successful Consul registration and shows no error lines, and the only failure recorded for the workload is pod admission being forbidden by the quota.

One reading conflicts with search being unavailable: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="search"} in namespace hotel-reservation reported 1 at 01:45:15Z. That is a single kube-state-metrics scrape point, while the Deployment's own Available=False condition (01:45:03Z), the absent search pod (01:45:17Z pod list), the empty search Endpoints and the FailedCreate events show the workload had no running pod.

Give the hotel-reserv-search container an explicit memory request (and limit) that satisfies ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota, or relax/remove that quota; the same addition is needed on every other deployment in hotel-reservation, since all of them declare only cpu and would be blocked the next time their pods are recreated.

gaps: Who or what deleted the running search pod at 2026-11-24T01:45:03Z is unknown: only a Normal 'Killing - Stopping container hotel-reserv-search' pod event exists, no object is seen applying that change, and the change_history integration is not configured in this Run.

No search-side telemetry exists for the outage period - no search pod, no search server spans and no search error logs after 01:44:52Z - so the state inside the search service itself cannot be observed.

Prometheus queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total (labels exist for service_name frontend/profile/recommendation/reservation/user) returned no samples for windows 01:00:15-01:45:15Z and 01:42:00-01:45:15Z (status no_data), so error-rate metrics could not corroborate the trace-derived error counts; those counts are a biased Jaeger sample, not a request failure rate.

traces_search for service 'reservation' and service 'user' was rejected with INVALID_PARAMS by the traces gateway, so those services were only inspected through frontend client spans and Jaeger's service list, not through their own spans.

The kube-state-metrics point reporting search available=1 at 01:45:15Z stays unexplained (likely scrape staleness); no metric series covers a long enough period to show the search availability timeline.

ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate (scripts revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh) exist in the namespace but their contents/activation were not read, so no statement about them is made; rate and geo also produce no spans in the sample.
End-customer impact (e.g. through an ingress or external load balancer) was not verified; only the frontend's own span evidence shows the failing /hotels responses.
next_steps: Compare the intended state of ResourceQuota hotel-reservation/memory-limit-quota with the application manifests: it requires memory on every pod, which no deployment in the namespace declares.
Patch the search (and other) Deployments with memory requests/limits under the quota, then confirm the ReplicaSet creates a pod and the search Service gets an endpoint.
After recovery, watch HTTP GET /hotels on the frontend for the return of non-error status codes and the disappearance of the /search.Search/Nearby error client spans.
Enable change-history/audit logging so that future pod deletions like the one at 01:45:03Z can be attributed to an actor.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
